title: Midnight Chicken

items.raw: 1 tablespoon harissa or other chili paste

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and salt it all over. If there is time, refrigerate it uncovered for a few hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Grate 3 garlic cloves and the lemon zest into a bowl and mix with the oil, harissa, honey, paprika, and fennel.
Spread the onion wedges and the rest of the garlic cloves in a roasting pan or large skillet. Halve the zested lemon and push it into the chicken with the thyme.

Set the chicken on the onions and rub the paste all over, including under the skin of the breast. Roast 1 to 1¼ hours, until the skin is deep brown and the thigh reads 165°F. Tent with foil if the paste darkens too fast.
Rest 15 minutes on a board. Squeeze the roasted lemon into the pan and stir the onions and garlic through the juices.
Carve and serve over the soft onions with bread to mop up the pan.

notes.label: Heat
notes.text: harissa brands vary a lot. Start with less if yours is fierce.

notes.label: The onions
notes.text: they collapse into something closer to jam than vegetable; make extra.

notes.label: Leftovers
notes.text: pick the meat and toss with the onions for sandwiches the next day.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — it assumes this is the roast chicken from Ella Risbridger’s book “Midnight Chicken” (lemon, garlic, a chili-spiced paste, and onions underneath). Is that the source? Who makes it, and is there anything your version does differently?
